Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain, with or without contrast, is the preferred diagnostic imaging modality. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: 37-year-old woman with clinical diagnosis of Cowden syndrome presenting with palpable left breast mass; mammogram shows irregular mass with microcalcifications pathologically invasive mammary carcinoma, a recognized Cowden-associated malignancy. B: Postcontrast fat-saturated MRI in same Cowden syndrome patient shows mass enhancement corresponding to invasive mammary carcinoma with lobular differentiation; in-text notes breast cancers typically demonstrate mass or nonmass enhancement.
panels.attribution_text: Dragoo et al. PTEN Hamartoma Tumor Syndrome/Cowden Syndrome: Genomics, Oncogenesis, and Imaging Review for Associated Lesions and Malignancy.. Cancers 2021. doi:10.3390/cancers13133120. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 6.
panels.figure_caption: A 37-year-old woman with a clinical diagnosis of Cowden syndrome (negative for PTEN mutation) and history of thyroid cancer at age of 24 and Wilms tumor at age 5, presenting with a palpable left breast mass. (A) Mammographic examination demonstrates an irregular mass in the 3 o’clock position centered 1 cm from the nipple with microcalcifications (circle). (B) Postcontrast, fat-saturated magnetic resonance image of the breast shows mass enhancement involving 3 of 4 quadrants due to multiple confluent masses (arrow), which was pathologically found to represent invasive mammary carcinoma with predominantly lobular differentiation and focal ductal component.
in_text_mentions: age age of diagnosis in patients with CS ranges from 38 to 46 years old [4]. Although difficult to estimate, the lifetime risk of breast cancer in women with CS is approximately 85%, which is similar to that of BRCA carriers [13]. There are no distinguishing differences in the imaging or histopathologic appearance of breast cancer in CS patients compared with the general population [4]. On MRI, breast cancers typically demonstrate mass or nonmass enhancement on T1-weighted images, with noncircumscribed or irregular margins and suspicious washout or plateau enhancement kinetics [14] (Figure 6).

in_text_mentions: erebellar folia enlargement and fourth ventricular compression with tonsillar herniation. The lesion was iso and hypointense on T1-weighted imaging (T1WI) and showed no gadolinium enhancement (Figure 2A). T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) showed a “tiger-striped appearance” (Figure 2B), and on fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), the stripes were hypo and isointense (Figure 2C). Due to imaging and clinical findings, LDD in association with CS was suspected. The patient was referred to the genetic department, where a thyroid ultrasound and panendoscopy reported a thyroid nodule of Thyroid Imag

of iso- and hypodensity at the lesion site, but frequently, a type 1 Chiari malformation due to tonsillar herniation is reported as the only finding [4,6,15]. MRI is the diagnostic study of choice. On T1WI, it shows iso- and hypointense lesions with stripes, and in contrast, it can show the perilesional vasculature with or without minimal enhancement of the lesion. On T2WI, the white matter is hyperintense with hypo- or isointense gray matter, which is called the classic “tiger stripe sign,” also described as a tigroid appearance (Figure 2), with similar findings in the FLAIR sequence [15-20].

in_text_mentions: A 26-year-old woman was diagnosed with breast cancer from biopsy of an axillary lymph node. An ultrasound (Figure 1) followed by an MRI of the breasts (Figures 2 and 3) were subsequently performed.

. In Figure 2, transverse T2-weighted magnetic resonance images show multiple coarse calcifications in both breasts and a large, lobulated mass in the lower lateral quadrant of the right breast. Contrast-enhanced subtraction MR images (Figure 3(a)) and T1-weighted images (Figure 3(b)) show a large, macrolobulated enhancing mass with irregular margins in the lower lateral quadrant of the right breast. Finally, her sister's mammography (mediolateral oblique direction shown) showed massive calcifications in multiple, well-defined masses, some of them with adipose tissue, diagnostic of hamartomas.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 7 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G). A: Gross cerebellar specimen demonstrates Lhermitte-Duclos disease, a major manifestation associated with Cowden syndrome. B: HE histology of cerebellar LDD lesion demonstrates characteristic loss of granular layer and Purkinje cells. C: NeuN immunohistochemistry highlights dysplastic neurons in the cerebellar lesion of LDD. D: Synaptophysin immunohistochemistry supports LDD with increased neurosecretory granules in subpial neuronal foci. E: HE histology shows dysplastic neurons within residual granular layer, consistent with LDD. F: HE histology shows dysplastic neurons replacing the granular layer, typical of LDD. G: NeuN immunohistochemistry demonstrates dysplastic neurons replacing the granular layer with molecular layer preservation, supporting LDD.

in_text_mentions: The surgical specimen was reported as a pale grayish soft tumor with irregular thickening of the left cerebellar folia (Figure 3A). The histopathology report described a replacement of the granular layer by dysplastic ganglion cells, attenuated Purkinje cell layer, and subpial neurons in the molecular layer confirmed with immunohistochemistry positive for NeuN and synaptophysin, which are characteristic findings of cerebellar dysplastic gangliocytoma or LDD (Figures 3B-3G).

on with deep extension [1,2]. The characteristic histopathological findings of LDD are a relative conservation of the cerebellar architecture with folia thickness as a consequence of a diffuse granular and molecular layer, which usually contains ganglion cells of multiple sizes, morphologically dispersed cells, and an attenuated or absent Purkinje cell layer. In the present case, abundant ganglion cells were reported in the granular layer, in which the Purkinje cells were partially conserved, and there was a conserved molecular layer with small groups of subpial ganglion cells (Figures 3B-3G).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Clinical photograph of the tongue dorsum showing grooves and cobblestone-like enlargement, a recognized oral manifestation of Cowden syndrome in a case report specifically about Cowden syndrome. B: Intraoral clinical photograph showing multiple coalescent papillomatous lesions on the gingiva/teeth cervical area, the classic oral papillomatosis of Cowden syndrome. C: Clinical photograph of the palm showing a palmar lesion with keratosis, consistent with acral/palmoplantar keratoses characteristic of Cowden syndrome. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real-patient breast ultrasound frame with an arrow and color-Doppler box over a suspicious right-breast lesion; the disease-focused Cowden syndrome article title plus in-text biopsy-proven invasive ductal carcinoma and the captioned spiculated/irregular infiltrative lesion support attribution to Cowden syndrome rather than an unassigned breast mass. B: Real-patient ultrasound frame labeled 10:00 right subareolar with measurement calipers over an irregular hypoechoic suspicious lesion; in this Cowden syndrome case the breast mass was biopsy-proven invasive ductal carcinoma, so the panel shows a Cowden-syndrome malignancy manifestation.

panels.figure_caption: Right Breast Mammography Showing Spicualted Opacity A spiculated opacity is noted in the right outer quadrant of the breast, causing local architectural distortion. No suspicious microcalcifications are seen. Mild skin thickening and nipple retraction are noted. Correlative breast ultrasound shows an irregular hypoechoic lesion with infiltrative margins at the 10 o’clock peri-areolar position, measuring 23 × 23 mm. Significant vascularity on color Doppler and intense posterior shadowing look suspicious.

panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E fine-needle-aspiration cytology (400x) of a thyroid nodule from the reported Cowden syndrome case. The caption and in-text document a benign hyperplastic/adenomatoid nodule with bilateral thyroid nodules (10 mm left, 12 mm right), matching the Cowden syndrome manifestation of multinodular/nodular thyroid hyperplasia (vocabulary synonym 'nodular thyroid hyperplasia'/'adenomatous goiter'). Disease attribution rests on the disease-focused article title ('A Pediatric Case of Cowden Syndrome with Graves' Disease') together with the specific captioned thyroid-nodule manifestation, which is a recognized Cowden/PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome criterion rather than a mere complication. Confidence is moderated by coexisting Graves' disease (a confounder for thyroid nodules) and the nonspecific benign cytology. No skin, ethnicity, or explicit patient age is stated in the caption or in-text (the title notes a pediatric case); only a scale bar is present, so no finding annotations.

panels.rationale: Single frontal clinical photograph of a pediatric patient whose anterior neck shows a visibly diffusely enlarged thyroid gland. The caption and in-text explicitly describe the diffusely enlarged thyroid gland as a physical-examination finding in this Cowden syndrome case, and the prior caption triage kept it for cowden_syndrome. Thyroid enlargement/goiter is a recognized Cowden manifestation and maps to the vocabulary finding cowden_syndrome_multinodular_goiter. The coexisting Graves' disease in the title is a confounder for a diffuse goiter, but the in-text lists the thyroid enlargement among the Cowden phenotypic features alongside facial trichilemmomas and abdominal keratoses, so attribution to cowden_syndrome is supported; confidence is moderated accordingly. Eyes are masked for de-identification; no clinical annotations are present.

The captioned breast lump corresponds to the BIRADS-4C breast lesion described in-text, i.e. a breast neoplasm manifestation of Cowden syndrome. The sheer size of the mass is an unusual presentation, hence variant typicality. Skin of the breast is adequately lit and light (Fitzpatrick I-II). No ethnicity or age stated for this figure. b: Real human-patient radiological image (mammogram-type projection image; in-text describes mammary CT) of the same right breast lesion shown in panel a, demonstrating gross calcifications and multilobulated contours of a BIRADS-4C breast mass in a Cowden syndrome patient, i.e. a breast neoplasm manifestation of Cowden syndrome. Mammographic calcified breast carcinoma is a recognized, typical imaging presentation in Cowden syndrome....

in_text_mentions: A complete colonoscopy performed by the referring physician revealed a macroscopically malignant tumor of the descending colon near the splenic flexure, which in the histological examination showed a high-grade intraepithelial dysplasia as well as numerous polyps in the entire colon and rectum, later confirmed by biopsies as hyperplastic polyps and dysplastic adenomas (Fig. 4a–c).Fig. 4Preoperative colonoscopic views: tumor of the descending colon (a), polyps of sigmoid colon (b) and rectum (c)
